question.problem: What is the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ with $f(x)=\frac{3x+4}{6-15x}?$
question.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{3x+4}{6-15x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{3x}{x}+\frac{4}{x})}{(\frac{6}{x}-\frac{15x}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(3+\frac{4}{x})}{(\frac{6}{x}-15)} \\  & =\frac{3+0}{0-15} \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote is $y=-\frac{1}{5}.$
